item.title: AOC Women's Forum February Webinar: Kellie Leitch, MD – Interim Chair at Mississippi: "It Starts With One"
item.dc:creator: scaladev
item.content:encoded: Register Now The Hon. Dr. Khristinn Kellie Leitch is the new interim Chair of Orthopaedics & Rehabilitation at the University of Mississippi Medical Center and an Associate Professor in the School of Medicine. Her current pediatric orthopedic practice focuses on pediatric trauma and lower extremity reconstruction. In addition, she is an adjunct Professor at the University of Mississippi School of Business. At the Ole Miss Business School she is leads a course in health systems management. Dr. Leitch was the Member of Parliament for Simcoe—Grey in the Canadian Parliament from 2011 to 2019. From 2013 – 2015 she served as Canada’s Minister of Labour and Minister of Status of Women, as well as serving on the Treasury Board and Economic Committees of Cabinet within the Government of Canada. Dr. Leitch earned her Doctorate of Medicine from the University of Toronto in 1994 and her MBA from Dalhousie University in 1998. She completed her Orthopaedic Surgery Residency at University of Toronto and Paediatric Orthopaedic Fellowship at Children’s Hospital of Los Angeles/University of Southern California in 2001 and 2002 respectively. In addition to her work as a surgeon and a professor, Dr. Leitch is a current Board member of the Dream Office REIT, she is also the former Chair of the Ivey Centre for Health Innovation and Leadership at the Ivey School of Business, University of Western Ontario. She has served on the National Research Council of Canada, Genome Canada, the YMCA (Greater Toronto Area), and is the Founder of The Sandbox Project: a Canadian charity aimed at improving child and youth health in Canada. Dr. Leitch was selected as one of Canada’s Top 40 Under 40 for her work in both medicine and business in 2005. In 2010, she received the Order of Ontario for her work advocating for children and youth.

O’Connor, MD is co-founder and Chief Medical Officer of Vori Health, a physician-led virtual musculoskeletal company on a mission to empower all humanity to lead a healthier life. Vori Health focuses on a biopsychosocial model of care delivery to help patients obtain the right care for their spine, bone and joint conditions. Dr. O’Connor is a nationally recognized leader in health equity, chairing the Movement is Life Caucus, a nonprofit multi-stakeholder coalition committed to addressing musculoskeletal health disparities, since its inception in 2010. She has long championed diversity and inclusion in orthopedics and broken many barriers to women in the overwhelmingly male profession. Her book, “Taking Care of You: The Empowered Woman’s Guide to Better Health,” will be published by Mayo Clinic Press/Simon & Schuster in October 2022. Dr. O’Connor is Professor Emerita of Orthopedics at Mayo Clinic and practiced at Mayo Clinic in Florida until 2015 during which time she served in many leadership roles including Chair, Orthopedic Surgery Department (Florida) and Medical Director, Office of Integrity and Compliance (Mayo enterprise). In 2015, she became Professor of Orthopaedics and Rehabilitation at Yale School of Medicine and the inaugural Director of the Center for Musculoskeletal Care at Yale School of Medicine and Yale New Haven Health. Dr. O’Connor left her surgical practice and academic medicine to embraced her entrepreneurial spirit and join Vori Health full-time in February of 2021. Dr. O’Connor is an Olympian (US Women’s Rowing) and is passionate in her promotion of the power of movement to improve health. JOIN US FOR OUR NEXT WEBINAR (click below to register):

I was trained how to do everything but run a lab!

MONDAY, June 13 • 1:00pm ET / 12:00pm CT

Researchers and surgeons spend years training how to run experiments, write papers, and treat patients. In their first faculty positions, they are often thrust into positions of managing a laboratory full of personnel and equipment, but with little or no training.  In this multi-part series, Dr. Guilak will provide information and advice on starting and running a research lab, focusing on topics such as personnel management and lab organization. Future topics will go in depth on other topics such as managing laboratory finances, effective grant writing, and mentoring.

This series is available to all AOCConnect members at no cost.

Dr. Guilak is the Chief Scientific & Innovation Officer of AOCConnect, and the Mildred B. Simon Professor of Orthopaedic Surgery at Washington University in St. Louis and Shriner’s Hospital for Children – St. Louis.  For the past 25 years, he has been principal investigator of a laboratory of 25-30 students, fellows, and staff performing a range of basic and translational research in orthopaedic research.

  • Utilizing resources within the CMS website.
  • Understanding the importance of Local Coverage Determination (LCD) guidelines for coverage criteria.

  • How to keep your workflows aligned with DMEPOS policy updates (competitive bid, same/similar, prior authorization, etc.).

Conflict Resolution with Tamara Furman

WEDNESDAY, September 28 • 8:00pm ET / 7:00pm CT

Tamara is a co-founder of SD Leadership Institute, a certified woman-owned business that delivers individual and group executive coaching, talent optimization tools and strategies, and leadership development facilitation. In June of 2022 the leadership of Duke Orthopaedics approached leadership about changing the policies for intaking patients across the ambulatory platform.  Our proposal was to more efficiently tailor what documentation needed to be collected on each patient encounter to avoid redundancy and then to develop processes so patients could deliver the information to us in advance of the visit.  The end goal is to reduce charting burden for front desk and clinical staff and to move patients more efficiently through clinic while improving accuracy and amount of information we collect for research and clinical care.  During this presentation we will talk about the process of meeting getting approval for and then implementing this several stage approach to change.  We will also show data reflecting on our current successes and how this affects our clinical operations.
